title: "An r-universe package in the lockfile can vanish without an archive"
ref: RNV-05
categories: [renv and installation]

attendu: "the recorded version, reinstallable at any time"

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```text
renv.lock:
  "mypackage": {
    "Package": "mypackage",
    "Version": "0.3.1",
    "Source": "Repository",
    "Repository": "https://myorg.r-universe.dev"
  }
```

```r
renv::restore()
```
:::

This pitfall depends on a remote repository that changes over time, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

An r-universe repository is rebuilt from the default branch of the git repositories. It only serves the latest version of each package, with no archive folder like CRAN's. As soon as `0.3.2` is published, `0.3.1` can no longer be downloaded from r-universe.

Yet the lockfile still points to that version. `restore()` cannot find it any more, although nothing has changed in the project.

## The remedy

Record non-CRAN packages by their git source and commit, which {renv} knows how to retrieve, rather than by an r-universe repository.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
renv::install("myorg/mypackage@v0.3.1")
renv::snapshot()
```
:::
